::: {.why}
A single cost number cannot be improved because you cannot tell which part of it is wrong, and separating the components is what lets phase 9 replace one of them without touching the others.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Return a cost breakdown by component from the engine rather than a single number.
- State which components are measured, which estimated and which assumed, for your own book.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Restructure qlib/costs.py so each component is a separate function behind a common interface, and the engine records the breakdown per fill into fills.parquet: half-spread, impact, commission, borrow, financing. The result object then reports the annual total by component.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Produce the attribution table for both strategies: cost in basis points a year per component, with a column stating whether each is measured, estimated or assumed. That last column is the honest part and it is what makes the milestone credible.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Costs are recorded per fill and per component in fills.parquet, so the strategy's cost can be attributed rather than only totalled. Phase 9 replaces the impact component with a fitted one and nothing else changes.
:::

## Resources

- [Almgren & Chriss (2000) — Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions](https://www.smallake.kr/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/optliq.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [Amihud (2002) — Illiquidity and stock returns](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A per-component cost breakdown in the result object, with the measured-estimated-assumed attribution table for both strategies.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Of your five cost components, which are you actually measuring, and what would it take to measure a second one?
:::
